Generator step-up transformers are specifically identified as qualifying manufactured products under this framework. Rehabilitation projects may also qualify under the “80/20 retrofit rule,” which allows facilities with at least 80% new investment to access the bonus, though any reused components are treated as zero for domestic content purposes. For projects seeking to claim the investment or production tax credits and which begin construction in 2026 or later, the OBBBA tightened restrictions on procurement from foreign entities of concern, including most entities in China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran, adding both new compliance obligations and opportunities for U.S. suppliers. While these measures reduce uncertainty and strengthen incentives for reshoring, gaps remain. Hydropower-specific manufactured components such as turbines, generators, and governors still lack clearly defined cost percentages in the safe harbor framework, leaving developers with partial ambiguity when seeking to qualify for the bonus. vii This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. In the interim, hydropower operators are taking adaptive measures, such as placing transformer orders earlier, sharing spare units, and phasing modernization schedules. Yet these stopgaps cannot fully offset the risks posed by systemic bottlenecks. Building new manufacturing capacity, reestablishing domestic expertise in large transformer production, and strengthening supply resilience will require sustained effort and coordination across government, utilities, and private industry. Ultimately, securing the LPT supply chain for hydropower rehabilitation is not merely a technical or economic challenge; it is a matter of national security. Hydropower provides a reliable and flexible source of generation that underpins grid stability. Ensuring timely access to transformers and secondary components is essential to sustaining this role. Federal support, industry partnerships, and proactive investment are critical to ensuring that the U.S. hydropower sector can continue to modernize and expand in line with the nation’s energy security and grid reliability goals. viii This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications.
